title: Section 230: Everything You Need to Know -- Tweets, Free Speech, Beyond

reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6C Podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6C Podcast. I'm Sonal, and I'm sharing our special episode on all things, Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, CDA, in what wired. And our expert guest is Mike Maznick, founder and editor-in-chief of TechDirt, who has long covered these and related issues.

key_points.text: I'm Sonal, and I'm sharing our special episode on all things, Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, CDA, in what wired.
key_points.evidence_quote: I'm Sonal, and I'm sharing our special episode on all things, Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, CDA, in what wired, a senior writer there specifically, described as, quote, one of the clearest but still nuanced explainers I've heard and is worth listening to.

key_points.text: We also discuss how does this law play out against broader questions and debates around platforms and content moderation.
key_points.evidence_quote: We also discuss how does this law play out against broader questions and debates around platforms and content moderation, but we begin with explaining Section 230 of the 1996 Act, which make sure that interactive of websites are not liable for their users' content.

key_points.text: Precisely, what does and doesn't it say, given lots of confusion out there.
key_points.evidence_quote: Precisely, what does and doesn't it say, given lots of confusion out there.

key_points.text: The law is actually very short and very simple and very straightforward.
key_points.evidence_quote: The law is actually very short and very simple and very straightforward, and I should note that the Communications Decency Act itself did have many more things that it did, but all of that was determined to be unconstitutional.

thesis: The episode explains that Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act protects interactive computer services from liability for third-party content and grants them the right to moderate that content without losing that protection. The discussion highlights that the distinction between a 'platform' and a 'publisher' is meaningless under the law, as Section 230 applies to any interactive computer service hosting third-party content regardless of moderation choices.
